clue.text: Acting up? On the contrary, failing to achieve potential

parts.note: the reverse of up, so the word for below is wanted here

explanation.surface: A puzzled critic wonders whether a weak actor is overdoing it or doing too little.
explanation.walkthrough: Acting up would be performing over; the clue asks for the contrary, performing under, run together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To underperform is to do worse than expected, falling short of what one is capable of.

clue.text: Serve him up with tripe cooked by probable successor

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients mixed up and transformed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook plans to feed a hated rival offal, cooked by the man next in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The heir presumptive is next in line unless someone with a stronger claim is born, unlike the heir apparent.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir presumptive is the person expected to inherit, whose succession is likely but could be displaced.

clue.text: Period of years when, say, Hitler lost time as a radical destroyer

parts.note: an era is a long span of time

indicators.note: lost means the letter for time drops out of the word for a tyrant

parts.note: Hitler is an example of a dictator, as say signals

explanation.surface: A history lesson about the years when a tyrant ran out of time as a revolutionary wrecker.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to pull out by the roots, so an eradicator destroys something completely, at its root.

clue.text: Petticoat Lane may slope down to water

parts.note: a slip is a woman's underskirt
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: Petticoat Lane, a London street market, apparently runs downhill to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Petticoat Lane reads as one London place name; split it, each word gives a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is an inclined ramp leading into the sea or a river, used to launch and haul up boats.

clue.text: Smell on board? Show who's in charge

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: SS is a steamship, as in being on board

explanation.surface: A captain sniffs an unpleasant odour aboard ship and asserts authority.
explanation.definitionFit: To boss people about is to give orders and assert one's authority over them.

clue.text: Couple of committee vouchers can draw circles

definitions.note: the definition describes the tool by what it does rather than naming it

parts.note: passes are tickets or vouchers granting entry

explanation.surface: A pair of committee members holding vouchers are able to sketch rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of compasses is the hinged drawing instrument with a point and a pencil used to mark out rings.

clue.text: Space fever? Just normal warmth

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move
to run a temperature is to have a fever

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether astronauts get a space fever and is told it is just ordinary heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Room temperature is the comfortable ambient indoor heat, around twenty degrees Celsius.

clue.text: Possibly relating to the whole

definitions.note: a noun phrase, where the answer here is used as a noun meaning a complete whole

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could form another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: A tentative description of something that concerns the entirety of a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun an integral is a complete entity; in calculus it sums up an entire quantity.

clue.text: Speaker skilled at splitting alternatives

indicators.note: splitting means the small word goes between the two alternatives

parts.note: or and or each introduce an alternative

explanation.surface: An expert debater is good at dividing the options available.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is an eloquent public speaker, someone accomplished at making speeches.

clue.text: Gang of Four maybe rush back to capture alien

indicators.note: to capture means the alien is held inside the reversed word
back means the word for rush is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A political faction hurries home to seize an extraterrestrial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gang of Four were four Chinese Communist officials; maybe flags them as one example of a group of four.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a set or group of four things, of which the Gang of Four is an instance.

clue.text: I'm a right heartless fool coming over for a beef

indicators.note: coming over means the whole string is turned round and read backwards
heartless means the middle of the word is removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: the word right with its middle letters removed leaves its two ends
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A man confesses to being a foolish idiot, coming round to apologise for a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef looks like a grievance or quarrel; it is the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is highly seasoned smoked beef, usually cut from the brisket.

clue.text: Mineral box

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crystalline mineral, such as feldspar
second meaning: to box or ... with an opponent

explanation.walkthrough: Box looks like a noun, a container; it is the verb, to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: Spar is a light crystalline rock-forming mineral, and to spar is to practise boxing.

clue.text: First form have field originally let out, which cannot be released

parts.note: class I, the first form at school

indicators.note: out means that letter is removed from the field

parts.note: the word field itself, before a letter is removed

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of let

parts.note: the first letter of the word let

explanation.surface: A first-year class may use the playing field, which is otherwise kept locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Form here is a school class, and I is the Roman numeral for first.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified information is officially secret and may not be made public or disclosed.

clue.text: Terrible spills around awkward bend — it is hypnotic!

definitions.note: a clause describing what the subject does, matching the verb answer in sense

indicators.note: terrible spills are a mess, so those letters are jumbled
an awkward bend is twisted, so these letters are also mixed

explanation.surface: A dramatic crash on a tricky corner is so gripping that onlookers cannot look away.
explanation.walkthrough: The two jumbled words combine into one set of letters rather than one sitting inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that spellbinds holds people entranced, as if under a spell, which is what something hypnotic does.

clue.text: Makes arrangements for future start of unnumbered gifts

indicators.note: unnumbered means the abbreviation for number is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone plans ahead to hand out gifts nobody has counted.
explanation.definitionFit: To preset a device is to set it in advance so it starts working at a later time.

clue.text: Gets the money back that firm kept in tatty purse

indicators.note: kept in means the company is held inside the jumbled letters
a tatty purse is worn and shabby, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to jumble

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves cash a company had hidden in a shabby purse.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to regain or recover money that has been spent or lost.

clue.text: Family row, years after

indicators.note: after places the years piece behind the row piece

parts.note: an age is a span of years

explanation.surface: A family quarrel still going on years later.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel, pronounced to rhyme with cow; it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineage is a line of descent, the ancestry of a family.

clue.text: Business advertisement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: relating to trade and business
second meaning: a television or radio advert

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes trade and profit, while the noun is a broadcast advert for a product.

clue.text: Cut the two talking

indicators.note: talking means the word is heard rather than read, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a pair is two of something

explanation.surface: A couple are cut off while they chat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to trim or cut away the outer edge or skin of something.

clue.text: I spread blame around; it is not under copyright

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the small word
spread means the letters of blame are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to scatter

explanation.surface: A plagiarist shares the blame, claiming the work was not protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitable means able to be copied, which is allowed for something that no copyright protects.

clue.text: Beak revealing what the charge is

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ... states the amount charged

explanation.walkthrough: Beak is also British slang for a magistrate, which makes the charge sound criminal; it is a bird's beak and a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is both a bird's beak and an invoice stating the amount owed.

clue.text: Is sent off to produce fillers

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dispatched to fetch padding material.
explanation.definitionFit: Insets are pieces inserted into a page or garment to fill a space.

clue.text: Sniff at the French wines coming over

indicators.note: coming over means the whole phrase is turned and read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone turns up their nose at imported French wines.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to sniffle or snuffle, as when crying with a runny nose.

clue.text: After good start, tragedy erupted over the ingenious devices

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of good

parts.note: the opening letter of the word good

indicators.note: erupted means the letters burst apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A promising beginning ended in disaster involving clever machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is a collection of gadgets, small clever mechanical contrivances.
